extracted.intended_audience: poets, dramatists, and creative-writing students studying craft and classical poetics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing poetry and drama grounded in Horatian principles: unity of structure, propriety of style (decorum), the balance of pleasure and instruction, character consistency, avoidance of artificial devices, and disciplined revision practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity & Narrative Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Works must cohere; parts should fit together and not produce mismatched or disjointed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity is the overarching requirement: avoid combining elements that do not belong together or that break the internal logic and tone of the piece. Tactics to achieve unity include appropriate beginnings (in medias res) and endings that sustain the work's form and tone rather than derailing it (avoid 'ending in a fish').

rubrics_metrics.name: In Medias Res
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin in the middle of things. Don't bore the audience with tedious origins. (Homer wisely didn't begin the Iliad with Helen's conception — ab ovo.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open at an engaging point of action or tension rather than with long background exposition. Use backstory sparingly and only when it serves the forward movement and unity of the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desinit in Piscem ('Ends in a Fish')
rubrics_metrics.description: Works must cohere. Don't produce mythological hybrids — beautiful at the top but trailing into a fish tail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid endings or late additions that are inconsistent with earlier parts of the work in tone, character, or genre; ensure the conclusion follows naturally from the established premises and internal logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum (Propriety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Match diction, vocabulary, characterization, meter, and invention to the genre and the speaker. Verisimilitude requires fitness — the form must suit the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure style, voice, and formal choices are appropriate to the subject, the characters, and the expectations of the genre; inappropriate linguistic register, meter, or invention undermines credibility and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dulce et Utile (Pleasure-Instruction Balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Sweet and useful.' Combine pleasure and benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for writing that both delights (aesthetic pleasure) and offers insight, moral benefit, or usefulness; the best poetry achieves both simultaneously rather than privileging one to the exclusion of the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aut Prodesse Aut Delectare
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry should 'benefit or please, or both at once.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this maxim to evaluate whether a passage is serving the work: if it neither instructs nor delights, it is superfluous and should be revised or removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Purple Patch (Purpureus Pannus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid showy passages of flowery language stitched in for their own sake — they break unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insert ornate, self-congratulatory flourishes that attract attention to themselves and distract from the work; such patches often disrupt tone and coherence and should be excised or integrated so they serve an aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Deus Ex Machina
rubrics_metrics.description: A god should not intervene unless a knot truly worthy of such untangling appears. Don't resolve plots artificially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist contrived, external resolutions that are inconsistent with the established internal logic of the story; plot solutions should arise from character and circumstance already set up in the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent Characterization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters' actions, speech, and development must align with previously established traits and motivations, or changes must be plausibly earned; inconsistency weakens believability and unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match Characters to Their Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Match characters to their type (age, station, region).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure characters' language, behavior, and roles are appropriate to their social position, background, and role in the narrative; implausible mismatches undermine verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety in Dramatic Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Special care for propriety in dramatic representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In drama, be especially attentive to what is appropriate to depict and how; respect conventions of the stage and the audience's expectations for credibility and decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Greek Models as Guides
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study classical exemplars for technique, structure, and craft, but apply those lessons with judgment rather than slavish imitation; models provide teaching examples for technique and propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set Work Aside to Mature (Nine-Year Rule / Nonum Prematur in Annum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set work aside; let it mature for nine years before publishing. Revise rigorously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow distance between composition and publication to gain perspective; use time for substantive revision and to test whether the work meets standards of unity, propriety, and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Common sense and knowledge of human nature; high ideals; intellectual rigor; willingness to accept impartial criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author should cultivate sound judgment, moral seriousness, and rigorous critical faculties, and must be open to impartial criticism to improve the work; technical skill alone is insufficient without sound character and critical discipline.
